thread:
jia: Quick run of kernel matrix for Llama2-13B q8_hybrid across h100/a100 in us-west1/us-east1. Summary below.

matt: drop the numbers pls (p50/p95/p99, tok/s @bs=1/8/32, est cost deltas).

jia: h100-us-west1 (flashattn v3 via triton + custom kernels): p50=22ms p95=46ms p99=82ms, tok/s @bs32=430, est cost rel=1.0

jia: a100-us-east1 (triton flashv2 / vendor kernel fallback): p50=35ms p95=74ms p99=138ms, tok/s @bs32=255, est cost rel=1.45

sofia: big p99 gap. did you try q4 variants and any CPU prep overhead comparisons?

jia: ran a small q4 sweep: h100 p99=76ms, a100 p99=122ms, tok/s@32=500/310. CPU prep for q4 increases prep latency on cold starts by ~8-12ms.

ben: what about quality impact? we need thresholds before changing routing.

jia: eval harness (1k prompts): q8_hybrid token-logprob drift median 0.6%, q4 ~1.5% with some safety prompts slightly worse. regen rate up ~2% on hallucination suite for q4.

matt: proposal: region+device kernel selection rules: switch to vendor fallback only if p99 > 110ms OR cost delta > 20%. require eval drift < 1.5% on critical prompt set. also add canary routing.

sofia: add hysteresis: require p99 to be above threshold for 30m smoothed window and an absolute jitter floor <10% before switching. otherwise we flip-flop.

ben: +1. also mandate a 10% traffic ramp for 24h with QoR + real-user-latency monitoring. rollback if QoR diff > 1.5% or p99 worsens during ramp.

jia: drafted a lightweight routing policy for runtime to implement: 
```
kernel_policy:
  check_interval: 60s
  smooth_window: 30m
  thresholds:
    p99_ms: 110
    cost_rel: 1.2
    eval_drift_pct: 1.5
  actions:
    - when: device==A100 and p99_smoothed > p99_ms
      then: prefer: triton_vendor
      rollout: 10% -> 24h monitor -> 50% -> 100%
    - when: device==H100 and kernel==flashv3
      then: prefer: flashv3
```

runtime-bot: [alert] h100-us-west1 flashv3 p99 +12% over 15m (investigate).

matt: can we reproduce with a steady-state synthetic load? jia can you run a bs8/16 2h steady run and attach flamegraphs + nvprof? block full rollout until we confirm.

jia: starting steady-state now. will post artifacts. ETA 2h. run id bench-1776009999.

sofia: also include a model fingerprint in rollout metadata: model_id + quant_config + tokenizer_hash so runtime doesn't mix variants.

ben: good call. add a cooldown after a rollback (2h) to avoid thrashing.

jia: (update) 45m in: steady-state at bs8/16 on h100-us-west1 shows p99 ~88-92ms stabilized, jitter 6%. nvprof shows occasional kernel launch latency spikes aligned with GC on host. uploading flamegraph link: https://artifacts.redwood/bench/1776009999/flame.html

matt: if host-side GC is the culprit we should fix infra, not kernel. but we still need the routing rule to handle long-tail until infra patch lands.

sofia: runtime implementer note: add 'safety' flag to routing decisions so we can opt out for critical models (e.g., customer X with strict latency SLA).

runtime-bot: bench-1776009999 completed. artifacts uploaded.

ben: next steps: 1) infra team to triage host GC 2) runtime to implement kernel_policy with hysteresis and rollout steps 3) add automated eval gate in CI to check eval_drift_pct before allowing 50%+ ramp 4) schedule a 10% canary for affected regions after infra mitigations.

matt: agreed. ping me if the 10% canary trips QoR or p99.

jia: thanks all, I'll follow up with a short postmortem if infra fix changes the baseline.
